candidates.bio: Alan Grayson is a Democratic candidate for Florida's 7th Congressional District. He served three terms in the U.S. House representing Central Florida, where he authored legislation on federal income tax thresholds, Medicare for All, and national flood insurance. Positions here come from his answers to the News Collaborative of Central Florida candidate questionnaire, compiled by Oviedo Community News and published July 31, 2026.
key_messages: Medicare for All is the answer to healthcare costs that are crushing people
No federal income tax on households making less than $50,000
Extend national flood insurance to cover hurricanes and storms, and let every homeowner refinance through the state at 1.5% lower interest
Raise the federal minimum wage, which adjusted for inflation is lower now than in 1968
Extend Medicare to cover every child until 18, and subsidize pre-K childcare the way K-12 is subsidized

campaign_themes.heading: Cost of living and taxes
campaign_themes.text: Calls the cost of living the second most pressing problem, saying most people feel caught in a rat race they cannot win. Would eliminate all taxes on driving, down to the tax on driver's licenses. Supports no federal income tax on households making less than $50,000, a bill he wrote while in Congress. Supports increasing the national minimum wage, noting it is lower now adjusted for inflation than it was in 1968 and would be $20 or more per hour had it kept up with productivity.

campaign_themes.heading: Healthcare
campaign_themes.text: Says healthcare costs are crushing people and the solution is Medicare for All, a law he wrote while in Congress. Separately, argues that every child should be able to see a doctor when sick and get all the care needed, so Medicare should cover everyone until 18, noting the cost is minimal because most children are healthy.

campaign_themes.heading: Housing affordability
campaign_themes.text: Says the cost of owning and keeping a home is skyrocketing. Would extend national flood insurance to cover hurricanes and storms, a law he wrote. Would let everyone refinance mortgages through the state at 1.5% lower interest rates, noting such a program exists but only 0.1% of Florida homeowners use it, worth more than $5,000 a year on a typical $350,000 balance. Calls the state insurer of last resort, Citizens, a disgrace that should be prohibited from operating at a profit. For renters, says federal programs that extend credit for building apartments should be expanded substantially, and that renters, who indirectly pay more in property taxes than homeowners, should get the equivalent of a homestead exemption.

campaign_themes.heading: Education and children
campaign_themes.text: Says the country is not doing enough to invest in future generations. Wants children off their phones and paying attention in class, special effort for special needs, and more teaching of subjects germane to living, such as how to find a job, pay taxes and stay healthy, in place of the details of European history. Argues schooling must recognize each child as a unique set of talents and limitations. Would improve pre-K childcare dramatically and subsidize it the same way K-12 is subsidized, noting younger people are having fewer children partly because they cannot afford it.

campaign_themes.heading: Democracy and executive power
campaign_themes.text: Names what he calls the looming Trump dictatorship as the top problem facing the country, and says the solution is to fight back by any means necessary, from impeachment to civil disobedience, and to name and shame.

campaign_themes.heading: Utilities and data centers
campaign_themes.text: Says data centers will require a substantial expansion of utilities and should bear that cost themselves, and that if capacity is expanded there is no justification for a price increase to anyone else. Identifies the real problem as the collapse of state utility regulation in Florida, arguing a properly functioning Public Service Commission would prevent much of it.

campaign_themes.heading: Environment
campaign_themes.text: Declines to name a single biggest environmental issue, saying government is responsible for clean air, clean water and clean food, for minimizing pollution and punishing violators, and for respecting and preserving nature and protecting recreation. Says the only opportunity to reduce climate chaos is through government action, because there is no Planet B.

campaign_themes.heading: Property taxes
campaign_themes.text: On the constitutional amendment to slash property taxes, says the collective decision belongs to the people and that if they decide through legal means to cut them, that is democracy in action. Would be against making up the revenue through service reductions, because state services are already inadequate.

Government must ensure clean air, water, and food; minimize pollution; punish violators; preserve nature. Climate action requires government.

top_stances.summary: Opposes Medicaid/Medicare cuts and rising premiums; backs negotiating drug prices and building on the ACA to lower premiums, deductibles, and surprise bills.
Prioritizes affordability: reversing recent health-premium hikes and tariffs, and adding oversight of insurance and utility companies raising costs on Floridians.
Supports tax relief for middle-class working families and opposes tax breaks skewed toward billionaires and corporations.
Supports building more affordable housing at all income levels and would ban Wall Street speculators from buying up single-family homes.
Backs Medicare for All, universal childcare, and affordable healthcare as core campaign priorities.
Pledges to lower costs for working families, including housing costs, and to stabilize Florida's home insurance market.
Calls for fully funding public education and trade/vocational programs.
